rounds.text: Jiya Eco-Products Ltd presents a compelling case for extreme undervaluation based on a massive discrepancy between market pricing and intrinsic value metrics [E28]. The stock currently trades at an EV/EBITDA of 0.27x, which is significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 9.22x, suggesting the market has failed to price in the company's operational efficiency [E10]. This is further supported by an extraordinary ROA of 1188.71%, which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 9.36% [E7]. While the market price sits at the top of its 52-week range, the reverse DCF analysis indicates that the current price implies a -50.0% earnings growth, creating a 100% margin of safety relative to the base case assumption of 15.0% growth [E4, E30, E37]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% and the ROE of 5.37% lags behind the sector benchmark of 14.84% [E3, E8]. Despite these points, the fundamental valuation gap remains the most significant feature of the evidence provided [E29].
